clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952 and purchase of the orchard, within the year: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, distance between June and Walter as he worked long hours, Glen's fights at school, Walter's cutoff from his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money, June's weeks in bed that first winter, rows between Walter and June over money for new trees, and June's shift down in anxiety as she joined the church choir by September. These shifts pile up from late spring 1952 through early autumn 1953 as the family settled into the valley.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failed, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when the late frost took the crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter's heavy drinking by June, conflict between Walter and Glen over blame for the loan, Glen and Marian's overfunctioning as they took over the family's money and talks with the bank by November, Carl's asthma attacks worsening that winter, Nora wetting the bed again in April 1969, Ida's heart trouble found and her told to stop working in May, and Walter's shift up in functioning as he stopped drinking and took work pruning trees by October. The family's reactions moved from the financial crisis through the sale and move to Ridgeport, settling as Walter began new work.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: Glen out of work most of that year sitting in the truck for hours, loud fights between Glen and Marian over money, Marian's overfunctioning as she took a second job cleaning offices at night, Nora stopping eating and losing weight that summer, Nora's distance from her mother as she kept to her room, Walter's drinking returning after six years off it, and Nora's functioning up as she ate again and made the track team by June 1976. The period settles as Glen began driving a delivery truck for the feed store in March 1976.

clusters.name: Wilma moved into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990 after selling her farm: Nora and Wilma clashing over the children's bedtimes and meals, Hollis working late and keeping out of the kitchen rows, Hollis taking his mother's side, Owen having tantrums at preschool, Wilma taking over Lily's care, Nora's eczema flaring on both hands, and rows between Nora and Hollis most nights. Marian drove over twice a week to take Nora's side. The period settles as Wilma took a flat in town in June 1991 and Nora's eczema cleared over the summer.

declined.reason: August 1994: Four days from the wildfire over the ridge to the family allowed home, with all shifts within those few days and calm settling once home within the week. This is an acute episode around a real threat, not a period.

1996–1997: A recount of the shifts leaves two that count: Tess's drinking and Rick's conflicts with her. The shifts told with always, forever or lasting do not count. The only change in the family among these events is Tess's own shift toward drinking, which is never an opening. Not enough in the diagram to choose a reading.
